name: blood-test-minicpmv-4_6-medreason
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4.6 (config.json max_position_embeddings 262144). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-08. A LoRA finetune of openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4.6, MERGED back into the base and uploaded as a standalone checkpoint (one model.safetensors, no adapter_config.json, no PEFT tag), so it is a full-weight derivative rather than an adapter. Training config is published in args.json: ms-swift 4.3.0, tuner_type lora, rank 16 / alpha 32 / dropout 0.05, target_modules all-linear, freeze_vit true and freeze_aligner true (card agrees: 'froze the vision encoder and trained only the language layers'), 1 epoch, lr 1e-4 cosine, 5% warmup, bf16, effective batch 16 (2 x 8 grad-accum), max_length 4096, seed 42, trained on the author's medreason_train.jsonl derived from FreedomIntelligence/medical-o1-reasoning-SFT. Architecture is inherited: hybrid-attention-ssm, 24 layers, hidden 1024, 2 KV heads at head_dim 256, 18 linear-attention / 6 full-attention layers, 262,144 max positions, kv_cache 12,288 B/token. PARAMETER COUNT IS IDENTICAL: safetensors total 1,300,428,016 on both this repo and openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4.6 - the merge added nothing structural. config.json is NOT byte-identical to the base's, though: the derivative ships transformers_version 5.10.2 vs 5.7.0 and gains top-level downsample_mode '16x', merger_times, patch_size 14 and merge_kernel_size [2,2], plus vision_config window_kernel_size [2,2] and insert_layer_id 6 and an explicit pad_token_id 248044 where the base leaves these implicit. Those look like newer-transformers serialisation, not an architecture change, but the record does not assert identical weights. EVIDENCE QUALITY IS WEAK AND THIS IS THE MAIN CAVEAT: the only benchmark is the team's own hand-labelled set of real blood-test reports, size not disclosed, and the card itself says 'small evaluation set, so treat the numbers as directional'. It is a genuine same-table comparison - one table, separate 'Base MiniCPM-V 4.6' and 'This model' rows, this model higher on all three columns - but it is a private task-specific split, not a public benchmark, and no shot count, prompt, decoding setting or item count is stated. Recorded as a contender on the strength of the same-table base comparison, not on the strength of the absolute numbers.
